newsitem.title: PERU: Malaysian minister arrives in Lima for siege talks.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian minister arrives in Lima for siege talks.

text.p: Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi arrived in Lima early on Thursday to try to secure the release of his country's ambassador to Peru, one of 104 VIP hostages held by rebels at the Japanese ambassador's residence.
Abdullah, who is expected to meet President Alberto Fujimori and other Peruvian government officials, made no statement to journalists on his arrival.
The Malaysian foreign minister was on a "special mission" for the "safe and early release" of ambassador Ahmad Mokhtar, according to Foreign Ministry officials in Kuala Lumpur.

The decision to send the foreign minister sparked rumours in Peru that Malaysia would try to cut a behind-the-scenes deal with the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas holding its envoy.

Despite the tough stance of Fujimori, who has flatly refused to consider rebel demands, negotiations between individual nations and the guerrillas appeared to be possible following the release on Tuesday of Uruguayan Ambassador Tabare Bocalandro.
The ambassador was freed after his government released two MRTA guerrillas from jail.
Furious at the apparent concession, the Peruvian government recalled its top diplomat in Uruguay on Wednesday.
Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said Bocalandro's release "made a solution of the case more difficult".
